raw_output: {"kind":"answer","urgent":false,"ask":null,"answer":{"cause":"The tank is empty, so the engine stopped because it ran out of petrol.","confidence":"likely","alternatives":["A fault in the fuel pump or fuel gauge, if it still won't start after adding petrol","A blocked fuel filter or a fuel supply problem"],"steps":["First, put the hazard lights on, then get everyone out on the side away from traffic and stand well off the road, never between the car and traffic.","Put on your reflective vest if you have one, and place the warning triangle behind the car at the distance this road requires.","Do not push the car along the road. Walk to the station on the pavement or verge, facing oncoming traffic. Buy an approved fuel can and 5 to 10 litres of petrol. See Nearby below for the closest fuel station.","Back at the car, with the engine off and no smoking, pour the petrol in slowly while standing on the side away from traffic.","Switch the ignition on for a few seconds without starting, then start the engine. It may take a few tries. Then drive to the station and fill up.","If walking there isn't safe or the car still won't start, call roadside assistance for fuel delivery or a tow."],"escalate_if":["You smell strong petrol or see fuel leaking under the car","The engine starts but keeps cutting out, or a warning light flashes","Any part of the car ends up in the traffic lane, or traffic is passing dangerously close","There is smoke or a burning smell"],"photo_observation":"The fuel gauge needle is on E and the orange low-fuel warning light is on.
